body:
# Feature request: optional symbol for categorical overflow summary rows

## Current behavior is intentional

The categorical `overflow` contract explicitly makes `…N entries` a **text-only** summary. The current renderer follows that contract. This is a request for optional additional representation, not a regression report or a request to change the default.

The implementation limits the symbol domain to the visible prefix and appends the summary only to the label list: [layout](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/1a515fa46d973fb99787ad2e1f7429fa5e4eb451/src/actions/guides/legends/categorical/layout.js), [symbol materialization](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/1a515fa46d973fb99787ad2e1f7429fa5e4eb451/src/actions/guides/legends/categorical/symbols.js). These files are byte-identical between the isolated candidate used for this observation and the integration checkout at inspection time.

## Source case

Source `0731` is a 429 × 438 chart with 44 country series and 906 original CSV string rows. Its initial Vega render shows 29 country labels followed by `…15 entries`. That summary row also paints a short line sample.

| Observed output | Original | ggaction candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Country labels | 29 | 29 |
| Summary text rows | 1 | 1 |
| Painted legend line samples | **30** | **29** |
| Preserved domain categories | 44 | 44 |
| Plot line paths / vertices | 44 / 906 | 44 / 906 |

The missing sample belongs to the summary row, not to an additional displayed country label. Its original stroke is `#bab0ac`, width `1.5`, length `5`, at source SVG bounds `x=340.5…345.5, y=428`. This equals the stroke of the first hidden ordered category, `Türkiye` (domain index 29). That palette color also occurs elsewhere; the gap is the missing symbol at this particular row.

The actual native legend configuration is:

```js
.createGuides({
  legend: {
    channels: ["stroke"],
    overflow: { maxItems: 29, summary: "ellipsis-count" },
    itemGap: 12,
    titlePadding: 4,
    labels: { fontSize: 10, color: "black" },
    titleStyle: { fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 700, color: "black" },
    symbol: { layers: [{ type: "line", length: 5, lineWidth: 1.5 }] }
  }
})
```

The native graphic has 29 symbol items ending with `Switzerland`, and 30 label items ending with `…15 entries`. Its normal legend placement differs from the source under the existing disclosed placement policy; that does not account for the absent painted sample. No source/native pixel identity is claimed here.

## Proposed optional support

Consider an explicit opt-in such as the following **unimplemented API sketch**, subject to design review:

```js
overflow: { maxItems: 29, summary: "ellipsis-count", summarySymbol: "first-hidden" }
```

When enabled, use the first hidden value in the final ordered domain to resolve the existing symbol recipe and encoded appearance, then paint that sample beside the summary text. Do not add a synthetic category, alter the domain/data, or reveal another country label. Omission should preserve today's text-only output and existing saved programs.

The implementation should cover creation, editing, overflow reset, order/scale/data changes, resize, save/restore, and final bounds/collision validation. Unsupported legend families should reject the opt-in explicitly. The initial supported scope can be categorical line samples; broader recipes need their own tests.

## Acceptance checks

- A 44-category / 29-visible case preserves 44 domain values and paints 29 country samples plus one summary sample only when opted in.
- The summary sample resolves the first hidden ordered value, including after reordering or changing the scale; it retains the configured sample recipe, stroke, width, and opacity.
- Existing calls and persisted programs still produce text-only summaries. No overflow, zero hidden entries, and `overflow: false` produce no extra sample.
- Source `0731` must explicitly verify all 30 painted samples, all 906 original string rows, and all 44 plotted paths / 906 vertices. Label-only agreement is insufficient.

## Qualification boundary

This chart is **held before admission and before any School request**. The strengthened proof fails with `source29-overflow-symbols-no-summary-symbol`. An earlier 1,070-check proof covered 29 country symbols, plot lines, and text but omitted the summary sample; it is retained as incomplete evidence and is not a full qualification. Original/native artifacts and failed logs remain unchanged. No source modification, tolerance increase, or missing-paint waiver is proposed.

Local immutable evidence: `reports/v13-source0731-summary-symbol-gap-evidence-v1.json` (source/compiled SVG DOM, native graphic/DOM, exact configuration, original failure, and isolated implementation hashes).
title: Support an optional symbol on categorical overflow summary rows

## Problem

A chart with a 13px heading and an 8px multiline subtitle cannot give the subtitle a 10px line interval. The default subtitle interval is 9.6px. Shared `lineHeight: 10` fails because it must cover the heading font size, even when that heading has one line.

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 360, height: 240, margin: 80 })
  .createTitle({ text: "Heading", subtitle: "First credit\nSecond credit" })
  .editTitle({ titleStyle: { fontSize: 13 }, subtitleStyle: { fontSize: 8 } })
  .editTitle({ maxWidth: 200, lineHeight: 10 });
// Chart title lineHeight must cover every visible fontSize.
```

## Expected behavior

Allow `createTitle` and `editTitle` to set `subtitleLineHeight: 10` independently. Keep the heading typography and geometry, existing shared validation, and all omitted output unchanged.

## Implementation scope

- One optional finite numeric `subtitleLineHeight`, at least the resolved subtitle font size, including a hidden subtitle's stored style.
- Subtitle interval precedence: explicit/stored override, shared `lineHeight`, then subtitle font size × 1.2.
- Explicit hard lines work without `maxWidth`; omitted edits retain the override.
- Keep the setting through subtitle removal/restoration, Canvas/facet replay, and serialization. Removing the whole title removes it.
- Existing concrete text and renderers remain unchanged.

The prepared change passes 40 related unit tests, the TypeScript contract, and a browser test measuring the same 10px interval in Canvas and SVG. Documentation, package, and integration qualification are still in progress. It is intended for the upcoming 0.0.24 release after the dataset milestone; nothing has been published or adopted yet.
title: Allow subtitle line spacing independent of a larger chart heading

A valid complete-axis frame edit can be rejected against the previous numeric title position. Labels move before the sibling title is rebuilt. Both the released-source runtime and the prepared 0.0.24 candidate reproduce this with three rows.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";
const p = chart().createCanvas({width:270,height:295,margin:{left:57,right:13,top:57,bottom:38}})
  .createData({values:[{x:0,y:6},{x:1,y:10},{x:2,y:16}]})
  .createLinePlot({x:{field:"x",scale:{domain:[0,2]}},y:{field:"y",scale:{domain:[5,16]}},guides:false})
  .createYAxis({ticksAndLabels:{values:[6,8,10,12,14,16],ticks:{length:5,alongOffset:0.5},
    labels:{fontSize:10,format:".2f",offset:6.5,alongOffset:0.890625}},
    title:{text:"Quantity",fontSize:11,fontWeight:700,offset:40.5,alongOffset:0.5}});
p.editYAxis({offset:4}); // throws: The y-axis labels overlap the axis title.
```

Constructing the same final axis directly with offset 4 succeeds. Actual SVG measurements show 0.953125px transient overlap with the old title, while the final title and labels have a positive 3.046875px gap. The earlier immutable program remains unchanged.

Expected: complete-axis edits validate the final same-owner sibling geometry. Genuine final collisions and focused label-only collisions must continue to fail atomically. Reuse the existing prospective materialization plan; no new API, persisted fields, or tolerance changes. Regression coverage should include canonical and named axes, restoration, persistence, and unchanged previous programs.
title: Validate complete-axis frame edits against the final numeric title position

## Problem

A valid Vega-Lite chart needs one six-item symbol legend combining threshold stroke color, threshold size, and an ordinal shape scale. ggaction currently supports only two-channel `color-size` or `size-shape` combinations, so this chart cannot preserve its legend through the public API.

Source: `vl_0198`, SHA256 `746b6f1e485ee629d630f84926ae85370544e7cd9b1d397374b3946b430b85fc`. The actual original renders **30 painted points**, one six-item legend, a **600×20 plot** and **685×135 outer frame**. No image inspection was used; evidence comes from compiled Vega, initial data/scales, SVG geometry and browser DOM.

## Source behavior

- Data is the original sequence `[0,30)`, yielding30 numeric rows.
- Size and stroke color use thresholds `[5,10,15,20,25]`.
- Size values are `[50,100,150,200,250,300]`; stroke uses six Turbo colors.
- The compiled legend has `stroke:"color"`, `size:"size"`, `shape:"shape"` and title `data`.
- Its labels are `< 5`, `5 – 10`, `10 – 15`, `15 – 20`, `20 – 25`, `≥ 25`; every symbol retains its corresponding color, size, shape and opacity0.7.

**Shape gotcha:** the source declares nominal shape with `scale.type:"threshold"`, but the actual Vega-Lite compiler produces an **ordinal** shape scale with domain `[5,10,15,20,25]`. Only exact values10/15/20/25 become square/triangle-up/cross/diamond; the other values are circles. Replacing shape with six interval bins would change the original chart. The original compiled mapping must remain authoritative.

## Public API reproduction

With one point owner containing the original30 rows, public X/Y, threshold color/stroke, threshold size and ordinal shape encodings all complete successfully. The following legend calls then fail:

```js
program.createLegend({
  combine: 'color-size',
  channels: ['color', 'size', 'shape']
});
// Color-size combination requires exactly color and size channels.

program.createLegend({
  combine: 'size-shape',
  channels: ['color', 'size', 'shape']
});
// size-shape combine requires exactly shape and size channels.

program.createLegend({
  combine: 'color-size-shape',
  channels: ['color', 'size', 'shape']
});
// Legend combine must be separate, size-shape, or color-size.
```

The source's stroke ownership must also be handled explicitly: a color-size circle-only legend is insufficient. Splitting this into separate legends or forcing every sample to a circle would change its design.

## Expected support

Provide an explicit public way to sample color/stroke, size and shape together in one legend, with unambiguous ownership and sampling rules across interval and ordinal mappings. Retain current two-channel behavior by default. Exact public API design is intentionally left open for review.

Mapped symbol area must stay consistent with each mark shape. Vega circle radius is `sqrt(size)/2`; a native area conversion cannot be applied blindly to noncircle shapes. Any implementation should independently verify all30 point geometries and the six actual legend samples, including opacity, labels and original scale ownership.

## Reproducible local evidence

- Original source/DOM: `tmp/v13-source0198-original-private-v1`.
- Actual original report: `reports/v13-source0198-original-private-readiness-v1.json`, SHA256 `2ff80c83b8eca18a09543d75702e31f91892a04f3cdabab58ab453894c54b759`.
- Successful public setup and three rejected legend calls: `scripts/probe-v13-source0198-combined-legend-v3.mjs`; report `reports/v13-source0198-combined-legend-probe-v3.json`.
- Held result: `reports/v13-source0198-essential-combined-legend-hold-v1.json`.
- Tested runtime: exact isolated package from commit `1a515fa46d973fb99787ad2e1f7429fa5e4eb451`.
- Current integration checkout independently has the same public `combine` union and the same exactly-two-channel validation constraints (`types/program.d.ts`, `src/actions/guides/legends/colorSize.js`, `src/actions/guides/legends/combine.js`); this is a source-code observation, not a claimed current-integration native rerun.

The chart is held before School authoring/admission, with zero School usage. No source/data/style changes, native fidelity pass or workaround are claimed. Two earlier PRIVATE setup probes were preserved separately; only v3 reaches the actual legend boundary.
title: Support a single three-channel legend combining threshold color, size and ordinal shape

For equal-width 2D bins, explicitly choosing between strict stored-edge membership and logical step-index membership would preserve both valid numerical interpretations.

With extent [-5, 5], 50 bins, an edge is stored as 0.6000000000000005. The input 0.6 belongs below that edge under the current [lower, upper) contract. Some datasets require the logical index floor(1e-14 + (value - minimum) / step), which places it in the next cell. Changing the default would alter existing semantics.

Proposed opt-in: `assignment: 'edges' | 'step'` on existing create/editBin2DData and heatmap bin options. Omission preserves current output and persisted snapshots. Only explicit step policy is persisted; editing back to edges removes it. No new action, renderer primitive, adjustable tolerance, raw-data changes, or default changes.

Full design, edge cases and regression requirements: https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/d6cef4fe/agent_docs/impl/bin2d-assignment/PROPOSAL.md

The minimal three-row reproduction and full 2,462-row independent simulation are recorded locally. The original comparison has 483 occupied cells versus current 481; the proposed policy independently reproduces all 483 cell counts exactly. This is numerical feasibility evidence, not a completed native or published implementation. Implementation and regression verification are in progress under prior project authorization.
title: Support explicit logical-step assignment for equal-width 2D bins

## Problem

`labels.flush: true` currently moves every label whose bounds extend beyond the axis span. Some designs flush only ticks near a mapped domain endpoint. A 300 px temporal axis ending in 2021 can have its last 2020 tick at x=290.3029232535547; moving that centered label by 1.4279232535547 px changes the intended layout even though the tick is nearly 10 px from the endpoint.

## Backward-compatible change

Add `flushThreshold?: number | 'auto'` to the existing Cartesian label options. With `flush: true`, a supplied finite nonnegative threshold limits flushing to ticks within that distance of either mapped range endpoint. Omission preserves existing behavior; `'auto'` removes an edited threshold. Do not alter data, domains, tick values, fonts, plot dimensions, or rotation restrictions.

Implementation and detailed design: [39aea9d7](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/commit/39aea9d7d94d9210f2e1df3c74a2c9569ef67753), [proposal](https://github.com/ggaction/ggaction/blob/2f6bf496b85cb0af8bf11ca40770510a92043216/agent_docs/impl/axis-label-flush-threshold/PROPOSAL.md).

## Verification and release status

The unreleased `codex/release1400` candidate passes 5,596 normal tests, 178 installed-package consumer cases, and 162 committed-source documentation/type checks. Source-specific preparation preserves all 224 raw rows, line vertices, points, and transparent rules; all eight representations render the same output.

Remaining: qualify the complete existing chart cohort before adopting the candidate, then include it in the synchronized 1,400-chart release. This issue stays open until publication and verification of the actual published package. The candidate's manifest version does not mean the feature is already in the published 0.0.23 archive.
title: Support endpoint-distance thresholds for Cartesian label flushing

## Problem
Panel headers currently follow one plot/Canvas edge even when mark geometry extends beyond a particular plot. A circle at the top edge can therefore approach the header more closely than an identical circle inside another panel. One common offset cannot represent different per-panel mark extents.

## Minimal public reproduction
```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";
const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ plot: { width: 100, height: 100 }, margin: 70 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { group: "A", x: 5, y: 5 },
    { group: "B", x: 10, y: 10 }
  ] })
  .createScatterPlot({
    x: { field: "x", scale: { domain: [0, 10] } },
    y: { field: "y", scale: { domain: [0, 10] } },
    guides: false
  })
  .editPointMark({ stroke: false })
  .encodePointRadius({ value: 3 })
  .facet({ field: "group", columns: 2, spacing: "plot" })
  .editCompositionLayout({ topLane: "shared" });
```
Expected opt-in behavior: the second header moves outward by 3px; the first remains fixed. Existing default output remains unchanged.

## Approved implementation scope
Extend existing header creation/editing with `anchor: "plot" | "content"`. Content requires plot spacing and uses the union of the plot rectangle and concrete semantic mark geometry, respecting strokes, translations, collections and clips. Opacity retains geometric layout stability. Along-edge alignment stays on the plot span. Axes, grids, legends, titles and extension-only graphics do not affect the anchor. Row/column overrides, rotated headers, layout/source/theme/metrics replay and editable persistence retain this intent. Field titles retain their plot anchor. Insufficient space rejects atomically.

The human has explicitly approved current and future in-scope questions for this translation/library task. Implementation remains on the local batch branch; public release is deferred to the next 200-chart checkpoint. This is distinct from the independent full-bounds wrapped-layout request in #258.
title: Support opt-in facet headers anchored to concrete mark content

## Problem

A single high-level faceted chart can resolve independent numeric scales with different tick steps. Existing fixed numeric format strings apply the same decimal precision to every child; `auto` removes trailing zeroes. A per-value label map cannot distinguish zero on an integer panel from zero on a fractional panel.

Original0581 has independent Y scales with ten ticks each: −0.15…0.30 by0.05 needs two decimals (including0.00), while0…900 by100 needs integer labels (including0). Existing public fold/computed/facet actions reproduce all223 unchanged CSV rows,426 defined line vertices, two450×300 plots at relativeY0/352 and497×753 outer dimensions. Exactly replayed source SVG SHA256: `f56774156c13aeb905720c36e03d9632605c6761f9b67187d169ad80a993e0a2`.

The original also retains ten malformed year strings and does not paint their line points. Existing public parseTime produces null aliases and line missing:'break' preserves this behavior without rewriting raw rows. An empty original change string numerically becomes zero; a public conditional numeric alias preserves the original empty string.

## Proposed capability

Add explicit axis-only `format:'ticks'`, retaining existing omitted/auto output. Resolve a numeric fixed precision separately from each axis's actual settled tick values, using its smallest positive step with stable floating-point normalization. Keep trailing zeroes at that precision and use the mathematical minus symbol. Numeric data, domains and tick positions do not change. Time/discrete axes reject this numeric format; existing explicit display-label maps keep precedence. Named axes, facade creation, focused edits, scale/data/Canvas replay, facets and persistence must retain and recompute the intent. Reject unsupported precision or ambiguous empty context rather than silently falling back.

This is a library requirement, not an acceptance waiver. No School calls or admission have occurred. Local unpaid evidence is in `tmp/total1500-0581-actual-original-source-capture-v2/` and `tmp/total1500-0581-private-native-capability-v5/`. Add focused pure/public/rematerialization/type/package checks and synchronized documentation before adoption; keep public publication at the next regular200-family checkpoint.

## Problem

Direct Cartesian line marks reject missing numeric coordinates and cannot preserve an intentional gap between otherwise valid observations. A translation must not replace a missing observation with zero, impute a value, filter it away and bridge the line, or alter the original input rows.

Reproduced on unreleased local candidate `c7cbee6f9d703b7f81b75894e1c2c90938353d5a`. This is not a claim about a newly published npm release. Existing area marks already expose an opt-in `missing: "error" | "break"`; direct line marks do not.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 500, height: 350 })
  .createData({ values: [
    { date: "2025-09-01", value: 4.4 },
    { date: "2025-10-01", value: null },
    { date: "2025-11-01", value: 4.6 }
  ] })
  .createLineMark({})
  .encodeX({ field: "date", fieldType: "temporal" })
  .encodeY({ field: "value" });
```

The final action throws `Field "value" must contain a finite number at row 1.` The existing strict default should remain; an explicit gap policy is needed.

## Real original-source witness

Vega-Lite family `vl_0549`, original specification SHA-256 `e3d484ec677b8fe43c067507ce5d96094e6936f30a3355bc37b92497fdddb847`:

- Two independently owned API tables: UK `raw.years` with 55 raw rows and US `raw.observations` with 945 raw rows. Preserve all 1,000 rows, keys, string values, metadata and order.
- The original US row at zero-based index 933 has `date: "2025-10-01", value: "."`.
- Vega-Lite retains this row and produces `defined: false`, breaking the blue US line. There are 944 valid US line observations, not a new observation at zero.
- A public computed conditional can keep the raw `"."` and derive a separate numeric column containing `null` at this row. The subsequent direct `encodeY` still rejects it: `Field "sourceValue" must contain a finite number at row 933.`
- This failure is independently reproduced using a focused `createLineMark` + positional encoders, avoiding the separate repeated-facade explicit-ID requirement. The gap limitation is therefore not an artifact of an ambiguous facade ID.
- The original shared frame is 481×362 with a 450×300 plot; original X domain is 1948-01-01 through 2026-09-01. No chart-size change, interpolation change or data substitution is an acceptable repair.

This family remains unadmitted and uncounted, with **zero translation-model requests**. No original or accepted historical chart module was modified.

## Proposed public direction

Extend the existing line options with opt-in `missing: "error" | "break"` on `createLineMark`, `editLineMark`, and the existing `createLinePlot.line` options. Preserve `"error"` as the default. This follows the existing area vocabulary and adds no rendering primitive or new action.

In explicit break mode:

1. Preserve original rows and source indices. Numeric strings still need an explicit computed numeric alias; do not add implicit coercion.
2. Treat absent/null position values as gap boundaries, with precise validation matching the existing missing-data conventions. Keep invalid nonmissing types as errors.
3. Split each logically ordered series into contiguous valid runs. Start a new subpath after a gap; never connect across it or fabricate vertices.
4. Apply the configured interpolation independently to each run. Define leading, trailing, consecutive and singleton-run behavior without invented observations.
5. Define domain inference explicitly: an otherwise valid X observation must not silently disappear from its axis domain solely because Y is missing. Empty usable dimensions must still fail clearly.
6. Keep aggregate, categorical, path-order, group/appearance and polar behavior explicit; avoid silently broadening unrelated modes during a direct Cartesian implementation.

## Acceptance evidence

- Strict-default rejection remains unchanged; an explicit break succeeds for supported direct Cartesian lines.
- Two separated multi-point runs produce two `M` subpaths and no bridge segment; leading/trailing/consecutive gaps and singleton runs do not invent data.
- Numeric and temporal positions, grouping and supported curve interpolation preserve original order and gap ownership.
- The real `vl_0549` row remains `"."` in the raw input and `null` only in its derived column. Both original API tables remain independent.
- SVG, PNG, PDF, semantic/graphic outputs, selections and saved program roundtrips retain the same gaps and source lineage.
- Public declarations, API cards and documentation describe the option and its supported scope. Existing no-gap charts and existing strict errors retain their output and behavior.

Implementation and package validation should enter the next regular 200-family release checkpoint, with all affected translations reverified against that candidate. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or publication.
title: Support opt-in gaps for missing coordinates in direct Cartesian line marks

## Problem

A wrapped facet can have a bounds-driven flow that does not align every plot in a logical row. The current facet materializer uses one shared Y origin per row. A single `gap` cannot reproduce a source whose second-row plot origins differ between columns while all inner plots retain the same dimensions.

This blocks source family **0944**. It is not admitted, translated or counted as complete. No model calls or chart-image inspection have been used for this diagnosis.

## Reproduced original geometry

The original static view has 72 unchanged CSV rows, four Country groups, 140 × 140 inner plots and a 406 × 445 outer canvas. The compiled layout is `padding:20, bounds:"full", align:"none", columns:2`.

Origins relative to the first plot:

| Panel | X | Y |
|---|---:|---:|
| England | 0 | 0 |
| Northern Ireland | 208 | 0 |
| Scotland | 0 | 192 |
| Wales | 208 | 187 |

Panel titles sit at the same title baseline, but the second-row plots are displaced by 5px because the layout packs full group bounds. The two shared X footer axes are independently positioned beneath the complete wrapped view. Date labels rotate by 60 degrees. An exact implementation must retain these owners and must not add one X axis per panel.

Original specification SHA-256: `b4ab0dcf7ee89027f5c80d5b76faf1681f97f75d814a9d19452593e9137c7a0d`.

## Current library behavior

Against local candidate `c7cbee6f9d703b7f81b75894e1c2c90938353d5a`, actual high-level `createLinePlot → facet → editFacetScales({y:"independent"}) → editCompositionLayout({columns:2,gap,spacing:"plot"})` probes with gaps 52, 68 and 80 all produce equal Y origins for Scotland and Wales. This is an invariant of the current row-track layout. Setting a different scalar gap cannot satisfy both reference origins.

The diagnostic uses actual materialized child placement and plot bounds, not renderer pixels or coordinates inferred from text widths. A smaller gap of20 correctly rejects insufficient header space; that validation must stay intact.

## Required capability and acceptance criteria

- An explicit source-neutral facet flow/alignment contract for independently packed full child bounds, retaining the existing aligned-grid default.

## Problem

Automatic linear axis ticks currently select the next larger step from the existing factor set. For domain `[0, 140]` and `count: 5`, this yields `[0, 30, 60, 90, 120]`. A nearest-step density policy instead needs `[0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140]`.

This matters for independently scaled facets. A six-panel example has domains `[0,140]`, `[0,110]`, `[0,180]`, `[0,110]`, `[0,140]`, `[0,120]`; its target tick steps are `20,20,50,20,20,20`. There is no uniform existing count from 1 through the 10,000-item limit that reproduces all six panels. Explicit tick arrays work for one unit chart but cannot express this automatic policy in a single canonical facet source. Facet children intentionally cannot be replaced independently.

## Proposed opt-in contract

Extend Cartesian axis tick selection with `rounding: "nearest" | "ceiling"` through complete axes, grouped ticks-and-labels, and focused tick/label actions. Omission preserves existing behavior and output. `"nearest"` chooses 1/2/5/10 decade steps at geometric midpoints; `"ceiling"` restores the current policy. `count` remains an approximate density, not an exact number of ticks.

```js
program.createYAxis({
  title: false,
  ticksAndLabels: { count: 5, rounding: "nearest" }
});
```

The policy applies only to automatic count-mode linear Cartesian axes. Explicit `values`, temporal/transformed/discrete axes and Polar/Parallel axes must not silently accept it. Inferred grids must reuse their axis owner's policy. Tick/label edits, named axes, facet replay, scale/data/Canvas updates, Basic/Full, persistence and package types need matching coverage.

## Verification and release

Prepare an explicit primitive/public target before implementing the option. Preserve existing defaults and numerical tolerances; verify literal tick values, geometry, malformed input atomicity, immutable replay, decoded PNG, browser/package consumers and documentation. The in-scope design is covered by the user's standing approval. This issue is independent of count-based domain rounding in #255. Development candidates remain unreleased until the next coordinated 200-family checkpoint.
title: Support nearest-step automatic linear axis ticks

## Need

Independent linear scales currently offer only boolean `nice`. The existing upward-rounding policy is useful and should remain unchanged, but it cannot express an automatic range based on a chosen tick density.

For example, this is valid today:

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({ plot: { width: 200, height: 120 } })
  .createData({ values: [{ x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 1, y: 108 }] })
  .createLinePlot({
    x: "x",
    y: { field: "y", scale: { zero: true, nice: true } },
    guides: false
  });
```

Its automatic Y domain is `[0,120]`. A count-based policy with density 10 should support `[0,110]`. When several facets need different automatic domains, one shared explicit domain cannot express the intended design. Changing only the tick labels would leave the data geometry wrong.

## Concrete proposed API

Extend the existing option with `nice: { count: 10 }`, without a new action:

```js
.createLinePlot({
  x: "x",
  y: { field: "y", scale: { zero: true, nice: { count: 10 } } },
  guides: false
})
.facet({ field: "group", scales: { y: "independent" } })
```

The count controls domain rounding density; it does not force the number of guide ticks. Keep omitted/false/true output unchanged. Require a positive safe-integer count and an exact one-key object. Restrict the object to supported linear position scales; reject it for other scale roles/types. Explicit domains retain precedence. Reuse the same immutable stored scale decision through focused/generic edits, data revisions, shared consumers, facets and persistence.

For representative input maxima `133,108,171,107,139,116` and zero-based domains, preserve legacy boolean maxima `150,120,200,120,150,120`, and support count-10 maxima `140,110,180,110,140,120`.

## Review and verification

The implementation review package is `agent_docs/impl/linear-nice-count/PROPOSAL.md`. Its executable concrete target and an existing explicit-domain control have identical graphics, SVG and same-run decoded PNG pixels; the new public option is not implemented yet.

Required evidence includes independent numeric expectations and finite-range containment, atomic validation, unchanged boolean behavior, explicit/constant domains, type changes, scale edits, shared/rematerialized consumers, independent facets, persistence, package/type consumers, and synchronized contracts/docs/generated references/examples. ## Problem

`createTimeUnitData` rejects a nullable field even when preserving the input row with a null derived calendar bucket is the intended design. This complicates faithful, row-preserving translations of charts containing missing dates.

Observed with the unreleased candidate `f507da9795004bc7142a998f0ef0880ac9c00040` while translating original Vega-Lite source `vl_1558` (source SHA-256 `cd4928195c37e9b9f71d52e4bbd2a103f4fe8f1f1d6465f6a4d42e96fd15f76a`). The two unmodified source tables contain 40,534 terms and 11,864 people. After keyed lookup and calendar-year extraction, 1,238 missing birthdays become null derived years; the remaining 39,296 numeric years are valid. All original raw strings and rows must remain intact.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';

chart()
  .createData({ values: [{ birthYear: 1745 }, { birthYear: null }] })
  .createTimeUnitData({
    id: 'buckets',
    field: 'birthYear',
    unit: 'year',
    temporalUnit: 'timestamp'
  });
```

The second row throws `Field "birthYear" must contain a temporal string or finite timestamp ...`. Omitting `temporalUnit` also rejects the null row. This is separate from #72's finite timestamp range issue and #167's computed calendar-year extraction support.

## Suggested extension

Consider an explicit missing-value policy for `createTimeUnitData` and `editTimeUnitData`, such as `missing: 'error' | 'null'`, retaining the current strict behavior by default.

With the opt-in null policy:

- Preserve every original row, field, raw cell, and row order.
- Map null or an absent optional input field to a null output bucket; preserve the input field as supplied.
- Retain errors for malformed non-null values, unsupported units/zones, out-of-range dates, and invalid finite/nonfinite inputs. Do not catch all validation failures as missing values.
- Give the derived field the correct nullable number/string schema for calendar buckets/weekday and retain input lineage.
- Keep creation, editing, persistence, dependency invalidation, Full/Basic entry points, and downstream null/unknown handling consistent.

Tests should cover creation and edits, mixed valid/null/optional rows, nullable schema/lineage and row order, an all-null input, rejected malformed values, and unchanged default behavior for existing consumers.

## Current translation status

This does **not** block `vl_1558`: existing `createComputedData` operations reproduce the exact frozen source calculation and singleton year-bucket result while retaining null rows. A real original-browser replay and an independent native probe verify all 40,534 point positions/paints. The proposed high-level calendar support would simplify this workflow and make it reusable without source-specific lowering. No public API change or release was made for this issue; the dataset uses the current verified local candidate and releases remain on the approved 200-family cadence.
title: Support row-preserving null calendar buckets in createTimeUnitData

## Problem

The existing continuous Cubehelix color controls reject `gamma: 0` and finite negative gamma. Two valid static inputs need 0 and -0.1; replacing them with the default changes every color.

```js
import { chart } from "ggaction";

chart().createScale({
  id: "tone", type: "sequential", domain: [0, 1],
  range: ["yellow", "red"], interpolate: "cubehelix-long", gamma: 0
});
```

Currently this throws `Scale gamma must be a positive finite number.` The same rejection occurs for -0.1.

## Concrete approved design

- Extend only the existing gamma value domain to all finite numbers, on Cubehelix modes only. No new actions, options, state owners or persisted fields.
- Keep default 1, existing positive results, `auto` resets, mode compatibility, clamping order and 8-bit input/output normalization.
- Gamma zero fixes segment lightness at its right endpoint, including `0 ** 0 = 1`, while hue and saturation keep the original segment position.
- At zero segment position with negative gamma, retain constant endpoint lightness and neutral saturation where applicable; bound the remaining extended RGB channels to bytes (NaN/negative infinity to 0, positive infinity to 255). This boundary is not a general invalid-data fallback. Nonzero-position nonfinite powers/RGB arithmetic still reject atomically.
- Marks, strokes, gradients, sampled legends, persistence, revision and facets share the existing mapper.

Source-neutral proposal, literal numeric targets and reproducible primitive target:

## Problem

Independent text marks support constant `dx` / `dy` in `editTextMark`, but cannot map a numeric field to per-item pixel offsets. A staggered calendar text grid needs different horizontal offsets for different rows while preserving its data grain and painter order.

`encodeXOffset` / `encodeYOffset` currently define categorical subgroup placement for bar/point/rule marks. They reject Text and have a different meaning from an unscaled pixel nudge. Splitting one text layer into several layers changes item order and adds unnecessary authoring work.

## Proposed public behavior

Add `encodeDx({target?, field?, value?})` and `encodeDy` for independent Text. Exactly one numeric field or finite numeric constant is required; signed values are logical pixel offsets. There is no scale or `fieldType` option. The three-key API follows existing direct numeric encodings.

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({width: 500, height: 300, margin: 80})
  .createData({values: rows})
  .createTextPlot({x: "hour", y: "day", text: {value: "⬢"}})
  .encodeDx({field: "shift"});
```

Include both channels in existing atomic `encodeChannels`, `removeEncoding`, data/Canvas/scale replay, persistence, declarations, inspection and documentation. An encoded component overrides its corresponding constant text offset; removing it restores the stored constant. Omitting one channel preserves the other. A field-driven offset establishes row grain even when text and both positions are constant.

Source-owned labels and other mark types remain rejected. Preserve input rows, final item order, unrelated encodings and existing omitted behavior. Validate finite numeric fields/constants atomically and retain existing Text missing-row policy. Renderers continue to consume resolved concrete text graphics only.

## Request

Offer an explicit Steffen monotone interpolation recipe for translating Vega/Vega-Lite charts, while preserving the existing weighted harmonic/PCHIP `curve: 'monotone'` behavior and every existing program's output.

Both implementations are valid monotone interpolators. The distinction matters for faithful translation: the same anchors and the same `monotone` label can produce different intermediate cubic contours.

## Reproduction and measured evidence

Compare Vega-Lite `mark: {type: 'line', interpolate: 'monotone'}` with ggaction `createLinePlot({x: 'x', y: 'y', line: {curve: 'monotone'}})` over nonuniform data such as:

```json
[{"x":0,"y":0},{"x":1,"y":1},{"x":2,"y":1.5},{"x":4,"y":5}]
```

The source Steffen and native harmonic tangent recipes agree at anchors but generally differ in their cubic control points. This is an enhancement request, not a claim that the current documented interpolator is invalid.

A current private qualification for original corpus chart `vl_1615` provides a concrete area/error-band case: 406 unchanged raw cars records, 398 finite MPG observations, 12 year groups, seed 1 with 1,000 bootstrap samples, and a 200 × 200 plot. All 24 lower/upper boundary anchors, fill `#4c78a8`, opacity `0.3`, and dimensions agree. The native area contains 22 cubic segments. Independently solving derivative roots of every paired cubic coordinate-difference polynomial gives a conservative full-contour distance upper bound of **2.483010776730733 px**, including the original SVG's three-decimal coordinate rounding and explicit floating-evaluation safety. This is an analytic upper bound, not a pixel-difference measurement or a claim about the exact maximum distance.

Qualification runtime: unreleased local candidate `c9d8d6eaf78c2cce5abfc3a2cd96d6db2a8a4e80` (package manifest still 0.0.21; not a new registry release). Original seeded source SVG SHA-256: `00b15b8cde5ccf5a527b32e8715fd17dc0d129250c93da1ee4285a11c1f0f9d6`.

## Suggested design and acceptance criteria

- Add an explicit, separately named recipe rather than silently changing `monotone`. Final public naming should be recorded in a concrete API design before implementation.
- Apply the selected recipe consistently to line, area, error-band, and explicitly requested boundary curves through the existing semantic actions; no renderer primitives should be necessary in translated code.
- Preserve the choice through Full/Basic facades, editing, persistence, and SVG/Canvas/PDF output.
- Verify every control point against independent Steffen reference calculations, including nonuniform X spacing, reversed area boundaries, repeated/degenerate X cases, and monotonicity. Verify existing `monotone` outputs remain unchanged.
- Keep the normal action/option budgets and numeric tolerances unchanged.

The current translation can proceed using a disclosed, source-bound native interpolation convention under the user's standing approximation approval. Exact Steffen selection would remove that intermediate-contour difference in future translations. Publication should follow the existing coordinated 200-success-family release cadence; this issue does not request an immediate release.
title: Enhancement: explicit Steffen monotone recipe for faithful Vega-Lite curve translation

## Problem

A line dataset can contain valid categories outside an explicitly ordered stroke-dash domain. An author needs an explicit dash fallback for those paths while keeping every original row, raw category identity, domain entry, and legend item unchanged.

The ordinal scale machinery already normalizes stroke-dash unknown values, but public field encoding rejects them, the shared consumer policy restricts unknown to other consumers, the focused dash editor does not accept the option, and `DashScaleOptions` omits it.

A minimal proposed flow is:

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';

chart()
  .createCanvas({plot: {width: 200, height: 120},
    margin: {left: 20, right: 100, top: 20, bottom: 30}, plotBorder: false})
  .createData({values: [
    {group: 'known', x: 0, y: 2}, {group: 'known', x: 1, y: 2},
    {group: 'other', x: 0, y: 1}, {group: 'other', x: 1, y: 1}
  ]})
  .createLinePlot({x: 'x', y: 'y', guides: false})
  .encodeStrokeDash({field: 'group', scale: {
    domain: ['known'], range: [[4, 2]], unknown: []
  }});
```

Currently the final call throws `StrokeDash scale unknown is not supported for grouped line or rule paths.` A late generic scale edit is also rejected by the shared consumer policy. A generic derived-data definition is not a value-producing workaround. ## Problem

There is no ordinary public data action for expanding parallel array columns into aligned rows. Existing wide-field folding rejects array cells, scalar nested-field access rejects arrays, and direct derived-data validation rejects `type: "flatten"`.

```js
[
```

## Problem

`createRegression` deliberately attaches its fitted line immediately after the source point mark. In a layered Cartesian plot, a line authored between the points and the later regression call therefore remains above the fitted line. Chart authors cannot express a last-painted fit through the high-level regression facade.

Reproduced against source commit 47270e126e881c378c3e66aa32dbaccecdc913b1:

```js
import {chart} from 'ggaction';
const program = chart()
  .createCanvas({width:400, height:300})
  .createData({values:[{x:0,y:1},{x:1,y:2},{x:2,y:1}]})
  .createScatterPlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false})
  .createLinePlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false})
  .createRegression({interval:false,predict:{values:[0,2]}});
```

Semantic mark order: `scatterPlot`, `linePlot`, `scatterPlotRegressionLines`.
Actual graphic painter order: `scatterPlot`, `scatterPlotRegressionLines`, `linePlot`.

## Existing working route

The public `createRegressionData` / `editRegressionData`, an independent line mark, and `bindMarkData` can retain a last-painted fitted line. This route has been verified with all source vertices and original data, so this is a nonblocking high-level authoring enhancement, not a missing rendering primitive or a reason to fabricate rows.

Creating a line directly on a regression dataset is not equivalent: placement infers its source mark, and fails when several marks share the source dataset unless a namespaced source uniquely resolves it. Binding an already positioned independent mark preserves its existing place.

## Suggested direction

Consider an explicit opt-in placement policy on the high-level regression owner, while preserving today's source-attached behavior by default. A plot-last policy should put the fit after existing marks while respecting grid/frame/axis overlay ownership. Creation, editing, data revision, source-following rebinding, selections/highlights, restore and export must retain the chosen policy. No renderer primitive should be necessary in ordinary chart code.

This would reduce several setup/binding actions and allow a high-level-first program to be progressively decomposed into the existing regression-data / line-mark route with identical output. A concrete API design and regression checks should precede implementation; no package publication is requested by this issue.
title: Allow opt-in plot-last placement for high-level regression lines

## Problem

The released public legend API offers `itemGap` as a uniform vertical center-to-center pitch (at least the largest sample height). It cannot express a fixed gap between the occupied bounds of adjacent variable-size rows. There is also no independently adjustable gap between a legend title and its body.

A source with explicit `rowPadding: 15` and `titlePadding: 20` therefore cannot retain these authored choices using ordinary complete legends and public edits. This is separate from an omitted default-spacing preference.

## Reproduction on ggaction 0.0.19

```js
chart()
  .createCanvas({width:520,height:600,margin:{left:40,top:10,right:180,bottom:290}})
  .createData({values:[0,50,100,150,200].map((v,i)=>({x:i,y:i,v}))})
  .createScatterPlot({x:'x',y:'y',guides:false})
  .encodeSize({field:'v',fieldType:'quantitative',scale:{
    type:'linear',domain:[0,230],range:[Math.PI,361*Math.PI/4]
  }})
  .createGuides({axes:false,grid:false,legend:{
    channels:['size'],values:[0,50,100,150,200],itemGap:15
  }});
```

Actual consecutive sample-center distances are all approximately **17.732309px**. Raising `itemGap` changes all distances together. `editLegend({rowPadding:15})`, `itemPadding`, and `titlePadding` reject unknown keys atomically. `labels.offset` is horizontal label clearance, `border.padding` surrounds the entire block, and block `gap` controls another boundary.

In the motivating source, actual source size-sample center distances are **28.5, 33.5, 36.5, 39px**. The source has 406 original car rows, 392 visible points, and categorical color, size and opacity legends with an explicit dashed frame. All 392 point positions, colors, areas, opacities and raw rows were verified using existing `encodeChannels`; the frame dash is already supported. This hold concerns the explicit internal spacing, not those capabilities.

## Expected direction / review required

Support content-aware row padding and independent title/body spacing using the ordinary legend ownership/edit lifecycle, while preserving omitted existing output and uniform-pitch compatibility. The concrete public names, precedence, persistence, all-family support and bounds behavior need a proposal and approval before implementation. No new API is assumed approved by this issue.

## Problem

Ordinary Cartesian marks are always materialized before axis and plot-border graphics. A source chart that composites a `difference` mark over those guides cannot currently preserve its backdrop through ordinary mark/axis/Canvas actions. This is a paint-order limitation, not a request to change existing defaults.

## Executed public reproduction (0.0.19)

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';
const p = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 240, height: 180,
    margin: { left: 40, right: 20, top: 20, bottom: 40 } })
  .editCanvas({ plotBorder: { color: '#ddd', lineWidth: 1 } })
  .createData({ values: [{ category: 'a', value: 6 }, { category: 'b', value: 9 }] })
  .createBarPlot({ x: 'category', y: { field: 'value',
    scale: { domain: [0, 10], nice: false } }, guides: false })
  .encodeBarWidth({ band: 1 })
  .editBarMark({ fill: 'yellow', stroke: 'yellow', strokeWidth: 4 })
  .editBarMark({ cornerRadius: 10, blend: 'difference' })
  .createXAxis({ line: { color: '#888', lineWidth: 2 },
    ticksAndLabels: false, title: false })
  .createGrid({ horizontal: { values: [0, 5, 10], color: '#ddd', lineWidth: 1 },
    vertical: false });
console.log(p.graphicSpec.objects['plot-main'].children);
// ['horizontalGridLines', 'barPlot', 'plotBorder', 'xAxisLine']
```

Moving the two mark edits after guide creation was also executed: the materialized bar layer still precedes the axes/border. `editXAxis({ zIndex: -1 })` and adding `zIndex` to `plotBorder` both reject unknown options; the original immutable program remains unchanged after both rejections.

At an opaque yellow / `#888` intersection, yellow composited with difference over the axis yields RGB `[119,119,136]`; drawing the opaque axis last yields `[136,136,136]`. Both are valid compositions, but they cannot represent the same source design. The source regression has all 53 stroked guides before its 12 difference bars; native output puts axes and border after them. Raw rows, monthly aggregates, all 12 bounds, gradient endpoints/stops and paint styles were independently checked before isolating this problem.

## Investigation

`src/materialization/graphicHierarchy.js` inserts an ordinary mark before the first plot-border/axis graphic and preserves that placement across later edits. Grid direction options expose `zIndex`; axes and the plot border have no equivalent ordinary placement option. Highlight bring-to-front changes item order within a mark layer. Extension graphics are not an ordinary semantic chart-authoring substitute.

## Desired capability / acceptance constraints

Provide an explicit, source-neutral way to place axes and/or a plot border before marks while preserving omitted/default paint order. The exact API and ownership design need review before implementation. Keep semantic ownership, immutable edit replay, canonical/named axes, facet/concat behavior and all export renderers consistent. Renderers should continue consuming materialized graphics, rather than reading semantic chart options.

Tests should cover normal and difference marks, default-output identity, guide-before/after placement, create/edit ordering, rejected-option atomicity, and exported SVG/Canvas/PDF paint order. This issue does not authorize a public API or architecture change.

Reproduction proof: ggaction 0.0.19 / commit `f6b50bf55a9de1857f106c7aa519326ce7a86d76`, reproduction script SHA-256 `0a29e3dfd33d823f91ab657a09ad85808665975e519f9108c3da3962ea34f89e`. No chart pixels inspected; no translation accepted through this gap.

## Problem

A compact, one-row facet cannot currently share its existing top margin between a parent title, column headers, and the upper Y-axis endpoint label. `spacing: 'plot'` adds the full header lane and parent-title lane to the complete child top margin. Reducing that child margin to compensate fails eager unit-axis Canvas validation even when the translated label would fit safely in the final assembled parent.

This is a request for a supported composition layout, not a request to weaken standalone-axis bounds checks or to modify a renderer.

## Reproduction (published ggaction 0.0.19)

```js
import { chart } from 'ggaction';

const rows = [
  { panel: 'Sun', group: 'a', value: 13 },
  { panel: 'Sun', group: 'b', value: 14 },
  { panel: 'Mon', group: 'a', value: 13 },
  { panel: 'Mon', group: 'b', value: 14 }
];

const unit = chart()
  .createCanvas({ width: 136, height: 262,
    margin: { left: 40, right: 56, top: 43, bottom: 19 } })
  .createData({ values: rows })
  .createBarPlot({ x: 'group',
    y: { field: 'value', scale: { domain: [0, 50], nice: false } },
    guides: false })
  .encodeColor({ field: 'group', layout: 'overlay' })
  .createAxes({
    x: { title: false, ticksAndLabels: {
      labels: { fontSize: 10, color: 'black', offset: 5.5 } } },
    y: { ticksAndLabels: { values: [0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50],
      labels: { fontSize: 10, color: 'black' } }, title: false }
  });

const parent = unit
  .facet({ field: 'panel', values: ['Sun', 'Mon'] })
  .editFacetGuides({ axes: 'outer', legend: 'shared' })
  .editCompositionLayout({ spacing: 'plot', gap: 22 })
  .editFacetHeaders({ fontSize: 10, fontWeight: 400, offset: 11 })
  .createTitle({ text: 'Grouped Bar Chart', align: 'left',
    titleStyle: { fontSize: 13, fontWeight: 700, color: 'black' } });
```

The current layout adds a 21px header reservation plus a 21px parent-title reservation to the unit's existing top margin. The user needs a target whose inner plots start at global Y=43, whose header text occupies Y=20..32, and whose parent title occupies Y=3..18. The upper endpoint label occupies Y=36.5..48.5. These global bounds are mutually consistent.

## Independently measured full example

In a seven-panel case, each panel's inner plot is 40x200 with a 22px plot gap. The target Canvas is 508x262; all seven plot origins are `(40 + 62*i, 43)`.

- Current API with a 43px unit top margin produces 508x304 and plot Y=85.
- Raw 14 input rows, UTC-weekday derivation, all seven partitions, and all 14 local bar geometries are independently verified. Maximum local floating point difference is 1.43e-14. This is a layout constraint, not a data-partition failure.
- Calibrating the original 13px title and 10px headers requires a 19px title reservation and 20.609375px header reservation. Preserving plot Y=43 therefore requires a 3.390625px unit top margin under the current additive layout.
- That unit is rejected by `createYAxisLabels`: `The y-axis labels do not fit the Canvas margin.` The final assembled upper label would nevertheless occupy Y=36.5..48.5 inside the parent.
- Plot spacing must be configured after outer-axis ownership is selected; the opposite order correctly fails an unrelated collision check and is not the issue reported here.

## Expected direction / constraints for design

Provide an explicit, source-neutral way to reserve a compact parent top lane using final assembled guide bounds, or another documented public lifecycle producing the same valid geometry. Preserve immutable programs, fully materialized child/parent snapshots, renderer independence, guide ownership, and strict standalone-unit checks. Do not silently shrink fonts, drop endpoint labels, move titles into mark layers, crop content, or change the inner plots/data to hide the failure. Omitted layout behavior should remain compatible unless a separately approved design says otherwise.

The exact API/core design remains unresolved and needs its own review before implementation. No library changes or chart acceptance are claimed here.

## Required behavior and decisions to review
A concrete source-neutral public/persistence design needs approval before implementation. It should cover:
- Opt-in plot clipping on the owning semantic mark, retaining all raw/derived observations and actual scale coordinates. Existing behavior remains the default.
- Immutable, fully materialized concrete clip bounds; renderers read graphicSpec only.
- Per-layer ownership: clipping the Point does not clip the three independent Lines, axes or external legend.
- Shared behavior across SVG, Canvas and PDF, including partial boundary glyphs, strokes, opacity, exports, rematerialization, inset/facet coordinates, serialization and replay.
- Coordinate/scale/Canvas edits update the clip bounds; disabling clipping restores the unchanged off-plot geometry.
- Regression controls proving that clipping does not become data filtering, scale clamping, or outer-Canvas clipping.

## Translation status
Only the affected family is held, before any school-model translation request. This is an actual public capability gap; it is not a failure to render the source. A separate source detail also needs deliberate handling: one reference line binds a nonexistent nominal color field, so the source paints no stroke yet retains an explicit two-entry legend. Current native nominal encoding rejects both the missing field and a null alias. That second behavior must not be silently replaced with invented source data or a fake legend mark.

No new public clipping API or stored schema is approved or implemented by this issue.
